collectr: Direct product links; numeric price API not configured
design: Pullfolio: charcoal zip binder printed with a different pixel sprite in every spot, reshuffled on each visit; the front-page search is the cover label in a stitched pocket the print flows around, with an index-card list and a name strip; clicking a sprite opens an info card about its trading cards, joined to the sprite by a yellow cable from a socket into a plug, (first and newest card, printings per year, languages); logo 4c in the site font; ring binder with multi-select language tabs, a set field and variant button that open a shelf under the toolbar listing only the Pokemon's own sets and variants with counts, a page slider in the Pokemon's colour with its sprite as the thumb, page turns, card pull-out and tilt; the pulled-out card has a cream card file with one TCGplayer price sticker, logo tiles for TCGplayer, eBay sold, PriceCharting, Cardmarket and Collectr, and card details (set, number, release date, illustrator, rarity, first found in, collector's note), lit in the Pokemon's colour
cardDetails: details/<key>.json from search/build_details.py: illustrator, series, first found in, collector notes, from PokéCottage's master sets
cardBacks: assets/backs: English, Japanese (1996-2001 and current) backs from Bulbagarden Archives, shown while scans load
collection: My binder: cards you own kept in this browser (IndexedDB), with JSON/CSV backup; value, paid and gain from TCGplayer prices; owned ticks on pockets; 'Mark cards I own' collect mode, Owned/Missing filters and master-set progress in every Pokemon's binder; a Breakdown by set, language and Pokemon that filters the binder, a daily price record kept in the browser (and in backups) drawn as a Value over time chart with the paid line, and Top movers over 7 or 30 days; Graded only, No price and Not in the catalog chips in My binder, Set my value for unpriced cards, and Find its printing for cards missing from the catalog; sync with a private GitHub repo (r12); the Value over time chart, Top movers (7, 30 or 365 days) and a Price history chart in the card file use each printing's weekly TCGplayer market price since February 2024, and a pulled-out card in My binder wears its own Pokemon's theme (r13)
priceHistory: history/<key>.json from search/build_history.py: one TCGCSV archive day a week since 2024-02-12, TCGplayer market price only (no mid-price fallback since r13.1) per product and subtype, rebuilt by the weekly catalog Action
prices: Our own: prices/<key>.json, built daily from one TCGCSV archive by search/build_prices.py (the source sits behind search/price_sources.py). The card file and My binder show TCGplayer's market price, else the cheapest TCGplayer Direct listing; the weekly history stands in when a day's file doesn't load. Chinese printings have no TCGplayer price. No price worker
browserCheck: r13.5: checked in Chrome, Firefox and WebKit at phone and desktop size. The card file keeps keyboard focus inside it, an Escape during the fly-out closes it, the footer no longer calls stand-in prices live, dates follow the language switch, the undo strip uses the phone's width, a picture with no stand-in shows the card back without a broken-image icon, and there is no tilt hint with reduced motion
catalog: PokéCottage's master sets again (r15), as up to r13.5: data/ from search/build_index.py, built weekly with PokéCottage's ids, English, Japanese and Chinese. Product ids PokéCottage doesn't give are looked up in TCGplayer's products via TCGCSV. Pullfolio is a non-commercial, friends-and-family project. Our own list (TCGdex + TCGCSV, r14) stays in the source as a standby
pictures: PokéCottage's scans first; a picture that fails falls back to TCGplayer's CDN by product id, then to TCGdex's (for printings both lists share), then the card back
credits: Footer: cards and pictures from PokéCottage, price data from TCGCSV, and TCGplayer's notice 'This product uses TCGplayer data but is not endorsed or certified by TCGplayer.' in English and Turkish
accounts: r16, in testing and hidden: opening ?accounts=1 once on a device shows 'Sign in with Google' in My binder (?accounts=0 hides it). Signing in is only needed to save a binder, never to search or browse. The binder is kept in Supabase (free plan, project jdorbiqrfeuoeaekowkw), one row per person, reachable only with that person's sign-in; the page holds only the public key. 'Delete my data' leaves a deletion mark that clears and signs out the person's other devices. Google sign-in is in Testing mode, so only invited Google accounts can sign in. A daily GitHub Action pings the project so the free plan doesn't pause. r16.1: ?accounts=1 also works when typed after the '#' (…/#my-binder?accounts=1). r17: with accounts on, a Sign in button sits in the top bar (a round initial once signed in) and the account card is at the top of My binder (Sign in with Google, or 'Signed in as' with Save now and More); a smaller empty-binder cover on phones. Signing out saves first, then empties the binder on that device (and turns GitHub sync off there); signing in brings it back. Unsaved changes are never cleared without asking r18: the account lives in a dropdown from the top bar (photo or initial, name, email, a saved-status pill, Sign out, Delete my data, and GitHub sync under Advanced) instead of a card in My binder; signed out, the same button opens 'Continue with Google'. Google shows its account chooser at every sign-in (prompt=select_account), so a second Google account can sign in. My binder's summary card is the total value, a $ | ₺ switch and a ⋯ menu (Download backup, Load a backup, Export CSV) over Breakdown / History / Movers tabs; on phones the sort and filter controls sit in a Filters sheet
